body.target_estimand: \(S_{\bullet u}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)=\{T_{\omega,\bullet u}:\omega\in\Omega^{\star}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)\}\), with \(S_{vu}=\{x_v:x\in S_{\bullet u}\}\) as its coordinate projection.
body.estimand_functional: For \(g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)=\bot\), \(S_{\bullet u}=\{e_u\}\). For \(g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)=g\in[k]\), \(S_{\bullet u}=\{W_{\bullet c}/W_{uc}:(u,c)\in P_g\}\cup(\{e_u\}\text{ if }z_u=1)\). Every vector is attained by one global minimum completion, \(|S_{\bullet u}|\le |K_g|+1\le q+1\), and \(S_{vu}\) is only the \(v\)-coordinate projection; the full matrix image is not factorized from the marginal sets \(P_g\).

sampling_model.design: Population exact identification of a joint intervention-column set from Yang et al.'s recovered real mixing equivalence class on their generic domain; exact rational encoding is used only for the separate completion-complexity results.
sampling_model.units: The population layer is indexed by the observed law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\). An optional region-union remark may start from \(n\) i.i.d. observations, but no first-stage inferential construction is a contribution.
sampling_model.treatment: The intervention fixes one labeled substantive variable \(u\), including a measured variable, a switchable group member, or a fixed singleton mleaf; all outcome coordinates are reported jointly before any scalar projection.
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition is used because the population target is a linear structural intervention effect recovered from the mixing representation.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The population theorem takes real \(W\) as the separable identification input. Rational \(\widetilde W\) is used only for exact promise-\(\mathrm{NP}\), \(\mathrm{FP}^{\mathrm{NP}}\), and block-tractability statements. Construction or alignment of a confidence region for an overcomplete mixing matrix remains outside scope.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Algorithm 2 enumerates all row and column choices and then retains the models with the fewest structural edges.
Theorem 3.3 gives a necessary-and-sufficient generic criterion for an observed-variable total effect when the causal graph is unknown.
Section 4 computes the observationally compatible causal-effect possibilities in latent-variable LiNGAM and gives conditions for uniqueness.
Theorem 4.3 certifies generic coefficient identification under general confounding by polynomially many maximum-flow computations.
The paper enumerates Markov-equivalent DAGs with linear delay and bounded structural change between consecutive outputs.
IDA computes possible intervention effects from local CPDAG information without enumerating every DAG in the equivalence class.

body.tldr: Yang et al. recover the real canonical linear LV-SEM-ME only generically up to a minimum-edge DOG class. This project separates a deterministic algebraic result from that generic observational-completeness step. For each intervention label \(u\), it gives the exact jointly attainable total-effect-column set: \(\{e_u\}\) for a fixed mleaf, and otherwise the normalized columns \(W_{\bullet c}/W_{uc}\) from globally minimum projected pairs, augmented by \(e_u\) when \(u\) can be an mleaf. Every vector has one attaining minimum model, the \(q+1\) bound is sharp on the published canonical, minimal, rank-faithful class, and each pairwise image is only a coordinate projection. The full matrix image is not factorized across group marginals. For rational completion, the promise decision problem is in promise-\(\mathrm{NP}\), optimization and search are in \(\mathrm{FP}^{\mathrm{NP}}\), and fixed within-block interaction width is polynomially tractable; unrestricted complexity remains open.

project_justification.gap: Yang et al.'s Theorem 3 identifies the mixed model generically only up to DOG equivalence, Section 5 treats one four-node effect, and Algorithm 2 retains a global minimum after a Cartesian enumeration. Prior latent-variable LiNGAM criteria omit simultaneous measurement-label and center ambiguity. No located result gives the exact jointly attainable intervention column, proves the sharp \(q+1\) bound in the published class, or classifies globally coupled rational minimum completion.
project_justification.niche: A total-effect column is local to the unique recovered group containing its intervention label once the observation-group partition and pivot normalization are explicit, but membership of a local pair in a global minimum remains coupled. This yields a complete joint-column map without falsely combining separately attainable coordinates or factorizing the full matrix image, while isolating computation in exact projected minimum-completion queries.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the deterministic joint-column formula and its generic observational-completeness corollary, supplies faithful attaining countermodels, proves that \(q+1\) is sharp, derives scalar singleton tests as coordinate projections, gives the polynomial oracle-to-image reduction, places the promise decision problem in promise-\(\mathrm{NP}\) and optimization/search in \(\mathrm{FP}^{\mathrm{NP}}\), proves polynomial tractability at fixed within-block interaction width, verifies the no-measurement reduction, and leaves only unrestricted exact completion complexity open.

body.related_work: Yang, Nafea, Kiyavash, Zhang, and Ghassami (2026), Definition 2 and Assumptions 1, 3, and 4 define the ambient real canonical, separable, rank-faithful, minimal class. Assumption 4 minimizes unobserved variables among LV-SEM-MEs with the same retained mixing matrix up to column permutation and scaling and the same observability indicators. Definition 7, Algorithms 1--2, Theorem 3, and Proposition 7 identify and enumerate the AOG/DOG class; Appendix A.4 supplies the invertible parameter rewriting and probability-one simultaneous preservation of Assumption 3 across the finite DOG class used for countermodels. Their Section 5 gives only a four-node effect example. Salehkaleybar, Ghassami, Kiyavash, and Zhang (2020), Section 4, and Tramontano, Kivva, Salehkaleybar, Drton, and Kiyavash (2024), Theorem 3.3, provide the closest latent-variable LiNGAM effect-image and complete unknown-graph criterion, but without measurement-label center changes; the present result reduces to the latter on the shared no-measurement generic subclass. Maathuis, Kalisch, and Buehlmann (2009) exploit local CPDAG choices, whereas mixed-DOG local pairs first require global minimum feasibility. Tramontano, Drton, and Etesami (2026) use maximum flow for a different general-confounding identification problem, and Wienoebst, Luttermann, Bannach, and Liskiewicz (2023) give linear-delay Markov-equivalence traversal; neither resolves coupled exact support minimization here. The present promise-class and bounded block-interaction results are partial complexity classifications, not a claim that unrestricted completion is polynomial or hard.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The marginal tables \(P_g\) determine every single-intervention column image but not the joint co-attainment of choices from different groups, so they do not factor the full total-effect-matrix image. Exact unrestricted \(\operatorname{CompOpt}\) remains unclassified because support in \(Q_\omega^{-1}\), \(D_\omega\), and \(B^L_\omega\) can cancel across interacting groups. The faithful plateau lies inside one interacting block: it defeats strict coordinate descent and additive per-group scores but neither proves hardness nor contradicts polynomial enumeration when every block has fixed interaction width \(b\). Population genericity is real and stratumwise; rational input is used only for deterministic bit complexity.
body.honest_scope: The ambient class is exactly Yang et al.'s canonical LV-SEM-ME with separability, Assumption 3 rank faithfulness, Assumption 4 minimality relative to the retained mixing equivalence class and observability indicators, and known labels. The joint-column formula is deterministic conditional on fixed \(W\), groups, and global minimizers. Equality with the observationally compatible minimum DOG class is asserted only on \(\Theta_{p,q,\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}\), using Appendix A.4's simultaneous probability-one faithfulness preservation; separability remains a distinct source-law premise. The \(q+1\) bound is attained within this published class. Pairwise images are coordinate projections, and no cross-group full-matrix factorization is claimed. For rational promised inputs, decision is in promise-\(\mathrm{NP}\), optimization and search are in \(\mathrm{FP}^{\mathrm{NP}}\), and fixed within-block interaction width is tractable, while unrestricted complexity remains open. No treatment-overlap condition is used. Confidence-region construction and mixing-matrix alignment remain external; only the definitional union coverage implication is available if a simultaneous first-stage region is supplied.
body.interpretation: The identified causal object is a finite set of whole columns. A normalized column records all outcomes under one and the same minimum model; its coordinates may be projected for a requested pair, but coordinates witnessed by different completions cannot be recombined. Singletonness of the whole column is therefore stronger than singletonness of one outcome coordinate. A nonsingleton scalar projection gives two faithful observationally equivalent models with unequal effects for that pair, while a singleton scalar projection certifies invariance only within Yang et al.'s generic minimum-DOG class.
